data.why: the interface's own shipped presets (src/agatesim/presets/*.toml) and archetype ladder are the real test material: 'Start from a form' loads a verified config directly in the UI, so no uploaded dataset is needed; the specimen-photo screen needs a real agate photo, which none of the stock images (bacterial/histology/gel photography) resemble, so it is left untested

goals: pick a target agate form (e.g. fortification, botryoidal, moss) and load its verified procedural preset to see the archetype ladder's reference result
switch the same form to its mechanistic tier (e.g. front feedback H1) and compare band corners, spacing and thickness against the procedural result
move sliders or use Randomize to explore how a model's key settings change the banding, checking whether a mechanistic draw still bands and still matches the chosen form
open the 3D screen, build a volume, survey random cuts, and judge how often a cut shows the target form the way a collector judges a cut stone
run a full-resolution run in the background and compare its saved slab, band statistics and archetype criteria against a pinned run

review.summary: The tree captures the main loop well: load a verified form, compare procedural and mechanistic models, randomize within the form, survey random 3D cuts, and pin and compare full runs. Every sampled screen matches its node, with one weak citation. It leaves out the timeline editor for conditions over time, which the README puts at the heart of the tool, along with hand-set parameters, tubes and specimens, and it needs a few structural and wording fixes before filing.
